articles.body: NEW YORK — Vice President JD Vance will hit a key hurdle in his fence-mending effort with Jewish Republicans on Thursday when he hosts a popular conservative radio host at the White House. 77 WABC host Sid Rosenberg, a longtime friend and ardent ally of President Donald Trump, has publicly attacked Vance for maintaining a friendship with Tucker Carlson, the former Fox News personality accused of invoking antisemitic tropes in criticizing Israel. Rosenberg, who’s known for making inflammatory remarks , has also taken aim at Vance for what he sees as the vice president’s lack of commitment to a “strong” U.S. alliance with Israel. In an interview Wednesday with POLITICO, Rosenberg said he plans to grill Vance in person about both Carlson and U.S. aid for Israel at a meeting he described as coming at Vance’s request. And while he said the main purpose of Thursday’s meeting is to get to know Vance, he noted that he’ll raise his concerns to the vice president in the context of his most pressing political priority: His likely 2028 run for president. “If he really wants to win in ‘28, he has no choice but to, at the very least, distance himself from [Carlson] if not completely disavow him,” Rosenberg said, adding that he believes the vice president “has pissed off the Jews and many Trump supporters.” Describing distrust of Vance in right-leaning Jewish communities as “a big problem,” Rosenberg said he’ll ask the vice president to commit to steering clear of Carlson and continue significant U.S. support for Israel if elected president. “I hope I can get some of those commitments. Do I think I can get it? I don’t know,” Rosenberg said. He added that he expects to meet with Trump in the Oval Office after his sit-down with Vance. As the front-runner for the Republican Party’s 2028 presidential nomination, Vance’s tense relationship with Israel’s supporters in the GOP could become a serious liability. Major Republican donors have already said they would be reluctant to financially boost Vance’s presidential run because of his views on Israel, a sharp departure from how Trump has held a commanding grip in that realm, thanks in large part to his alliance with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In that light, Vance’s meeting with Rosenberg — who has known Trump since at least 2018 — takes on outsize significance. It also comes after Vance extended an olive branch earlier this month at the Republican Jewish Coalition’s leadership summit in Las Vegas, where he voiced concern about antisemitic hate crimes and said working with Israel is “in the best interest of the United States.” Vance touched on Carlson at that summit as well, acknowledging that “people in this room may disagree” with things he’s said, but the vice president avoided discussing his relationship with him . Just days after that appearance, however, Vance ignited criticism from pro-Israel Republicans again by saying in a speech that the U.S. cannot allow its Middle East policy approach to be “subservient to the State of Israel.” Asked about Rosenberg’s comments ahead of their White House meeting, a Vance spokesperson said Wednesday that the vice president would be meeting with the radio host after they didn't meet in Las Vegas. “The Vice President was unfortunately not able to meet with him in Las Vegas during the RJC Leadership Summit, and of course wanted to make time to meet with him in Washington,” the spokesperson said. Rosenberg, a former sports commentator who now runs his own political radio show “Sid & Friends in the Morning” in New York City, confirmed Vance’s team asked for Thursday’s meeting. And despite his concerns about Vance’s Israel posture, he called the vice president an “affable” and “smart” person who’s “capable of the job.” Still, Rosenberg made clear he doesn’t view Vance as the strongest Republican contender for president in 2028. “He’s not my first choice. I’m a Marco guy,” Rosenberg said, referring to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who’s also rumored as a possible 2028 candidate. “If it turns out Marco doesn’t run, and JD wins the primary, in the end, if JD is the last man standing, I will support him.” Rosenberg’s influence remains mostly limited to the relatively small world of Republican politics in deep-blue New York. Still, his friendship with Trump has elevated him as a voice on the right, even as he’s attracted his share of controversy. In March, Rosenberg called Zohran Mamdani, New York City’s first Muslim mayor, an “America hating, Jew hating, Radical Islam cockroach" while voicing displeasure with Trump’s surprisingly cordial interactions with Mamdani. After drawing intense pushback from voices across the aisle, Rosenberg apologized to Mamdani for the harsh remark, saying it was a “bit over the top” and admitting it’s “not nice to call somebody a bug.” Rosenberg also came under intense fire earlier this year for calling Mamdani “a terrorist” — and apologized for that remark too. But he later retracted that apology , saying he was “exactly right” to use the term. With additional reporting by Alex Gangitano
articles.headline: JD Vance faces test in White House meeting with Israel-backing radio host

articles.body: JACOB’S LADDER: Otsego County Democratic Chair Caitlin Ogden is launching a bid for the top spot in the state party — the first time its current chair, Jay Jacobs, has had a challenger during his lengthy tenure. Jacobs, who also serves as Nassau County’s Democratic chair, has led the state party under the past three governors, with stints from 2009 to 2012 and 2019 through the present. But those stints have unfolded despite years of grumbling from the party’s progressive flank. “I came in as Otsego County chair about five years ago, and I’ve heard since then that Jay Jacobs has helped the party get by. And he definitely has,” Ogden said. “But I think the political landscape is shifting radically, and it’s time for a new leader to guide the party through the next phase and really deliver on Gov. Hochul’s vision of statewide, year-round party organizing.” The friendly footing toward Gov. Kathy Hochul is a bit of a shift for Ogden. She was a top supporter of Lt. Gov. Antonio Delgado’s challenge to the governor. But expanding on Hochul’s efforts to use the party to help candidates up and down the ballot is now the focus of Ogden’s message as she attempts to win over party members. The Democratic Party has indisputably played a larger role organizing campaigns across the state in recent years, though numerous local officials have characterized this as a slapdash operation that emerges only in the run-up to congressional contests. Ogden said that in 2022 she “had been expecting there to be a coordinated campaign structure because I had been told there would be.” “There was not in any capacity — there was no organizational help from Albany or the state party,” she said. “We never got any literature for any of our Albany candidates; we finally got 40 signs for Kathy Hochul in the middle of October.” The party apparatus has since been more helpful, Ogden said. But it’s still absent more often than not. It played no role as Democrats in her county had one of its best nights in history last November and has been quiet so far in the county that’s at the heart of Rep. Josh Riley’s battleground district. “We don’t even have staff hired yet, at least to my knowledge,” she said. “And it’s so late in the game.” “Is it something that would be helpful?” Jacobs said in response to Ogden’s call for a more regular statewide effort. “Of course.” “But the big question is ‘where do you get the money?’ We raise millions now: This coordinated campaign is going to run through between $6 and $8 million. And that’s not easy to raise, so speculating that you’ll be able to fund not only election year coordinated campaigns, but also ongoing coordinated campaigns year-round every year, I don’t think is reasonable.” Jacobs highlighted several accomplishments at the state party, such as a grant program that’s given $1 million to county committees and “allowing resolutions to come to the floor, where before they were always tabled to not allow for debate.” He also acknowledged that while 2022 was a “tough year” for the party, it did “very well” in 2024. The party’s elected committee members select the chair . But historically, they’ve just gone along with whomever’s picked by the governor — a potential obstacle to the pro-Delgado Ogden, but one she thinks can be overcome. “The conversation has been happening for a really long time now … about whether or not our leadership is on the right path,” she said. Jacobs has faced calls for his ouster after the 2021, 2022 and 2025 elections, and easily survived a vote of no confidence six years ago. There were rumors last fall that his tenure was at an end after he declined to endorse then-mayoral nominee Zohran Mamdani, but Hochul said he was “doing a great job” and the party stuck with him. “Since I’ve been the chair for ten years over two different tenures, I have heard repeatedly that I’m on the way out,” Jacobs said. “The only thing is, it’s never come from me.” “It’s not that I need it for my livelihood — I like being involved in the Democratic Party and I find this a worthwhile endeavor. So as long as that remains, I’m happy to continue.” The state Democratic Party will decide on Oct. 1 whether Jacobs stays on or not. — Bill Mahoney FROM CITY HALL ZO ON BIBI IN NYC: Mayor Zohran Mamdani spoke publicly for the first time today on his plans to skip the protests against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The Jewish head of state will be in New York City next week for the United Nations General Assembly. “I have made very clear about my views, my thoughts, my assessments,” Mamdani said when asked why he’ll sit out. “When it comes to the UN General Assembly, my focus is ensuring that our city remains prepared to host representatives from across the world, to keep New Yorkers safe, and also to ensure that we’re able to both address the global conversation and the very local concerns New Yorkers have about traffic and their ability to get from point A to point B over the course of the next week.” Mamdani’s nod to quotidian anxieties like gridlock is a far cry from his typically strident anti-Israel rhetoric and long history of pro-Palestinian activism. As recently as July, he was publicly railing against Netanyahu and entertaining the idea of having the NYPD arrest him on a controversial war crimes warrant issued by the International Criminal Court over Israel’s war in Gaza. The war, launched in response to Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack that killed about 1,200 Israelis, has left more than 73,000 Palestinians dead. Mamdani ultimately walked back his calls , saying in a social media video that his administration does not have the “independent legal authority to enforce this warrant.” Still, he has continued to condemn Netanyahu, whom he called the “architect of a horrific genocide.” And he has appeared to call New Yorkers to action, saying that, “while we cannot end the genocide on our own, we can decide whether our silence will become another weapon.” The mayor faced accusations that he was stoking antisemitism by continuing to talk about arresting Netanyahu despite knowing he lacked the power to do so . The mayor took a more measured tone today when answering questions about whether he would encourage critics of Israel to protest Netanyahu’s visit to the city. “To New Yorkers — I’ve never encouraged them to protest, but I always told them they have the right to do so, and we respect that right, and this city is proud of the first amendment,” Mamdani said. Regardless, sizable protests are expected ahead of and during Netanyahu’s Sept. 24 speech at the UN. The mayor said he has been in close contact with the NYPD and there are no expected security threats. — Molly Reinmann SEWER SOCIALISM: Mamdani’s administration plans to install 17 free public bathrooms across the five boroughs — part of a one-year, $4 million pilot project with the modular public toilet company Throne Labs. Each of the modular bathrooms will be climate controlled, have a toilet, a sink and a baby changing station, and will close at 10 p.m. To enter, New Yorkers can scan a QR code, use an app, send a text message, or use a physical tap card. “These 17 formerly bathroomless locations will soon become New York City’s number one place to go number two — or number one, you don’t need to tell me,” the mayor joked today. The pilot program is set to place five toilets in the Bronx, four in Brooklyn, three in Queens, four in Manhattan and one in Staten Island. The initiative builds on a January announcement from Mamdani and is an attempt to solve an enduring problem that’s bedeviled city officials for decades: How to construct a simple public restroom without taking years and spending millions of dollars. Former Council Member David Greenfield once highlighted a public restroom renovation in his district that — bogged down by municipal procurement and construction requirements — took nearly a decade and cost $2 million. The commodes announced by Mamdani today, by contrast, are projected to come out to under $250,000 per bathroom, inclusive of maintenance, for the year-long pilot. “We are essentially wasting taxpayer money,” Greenfield said at the time . “You can build a complete house in six months for $1 million.” — Molly Reinmann and Joe Anuta FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL EYES ON AI: Democratic Rep. Pat Ryan and former city Comptroller Brad Lander are among the signatories on a pledge to refuse cash from the big-money, pro-AI political group Leading the Future. Lander, who’s all but certain to serve in Congress next year after winning the June primary in a safe-blue district, said he’s “determined to pass strong safeguards into law and make sure the American people have a true say in the future of AI.” Ryan accused the “Big Tech oligarchs behind Leading the Future” of only caring “about their profits.” — an argument he made during the primary for NY-12 . In that race to succeed retiring Rep. Jerry Nadler, Ryan backed state Assemblymember Alex Bores, one of Leading the Future’s biggest targets . Bores finished in second place. The public condemnations from Ryan and Lander come amid heightened concerns about the existential threat potentially posed by AI. New York politicians have urged the federal government to do more to address the rapidly developing technology, and Hochul vowed that the state will fill the void in the absence of action from Washington. Leading the Future, which is backed by leaders at OpenAI and the venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, has pushed back against criticism that it’s anti-regulation. It previously stated that it supports “passing a national regulatory framework for AI.” — Madison Fernandez IN OTHER NEWS — GRACIE GATHERING: Students and teachers from two of New York City’s elite Orthodox Jewish schools will demonstrate Friday outside Gracie Mansion. articles.body: HELP! I’VE FALLEN AND I CAN GET UP: A report from the New York City Department of Investigation confirmed today what many political watchers have long suspected — that the city’s police pension system is ripe for abuse. The Police Pension Fund doles out retirement payments to all NYPD officers and, in fiscal year 2025, paid $935 million to officers who qualified for accident disability retirement — meaning they were injured on the job and unable to perform their duties. While DOI Commissioner Nadia Shihata said injured officers should be fairly compensated, her office found the pension system assigns this distinction — which boosts pension payments by 50% and allows officers to receive 75% of their average pay — without considering an officer’s specific job duties. “No New Yorker wants to stand in the way of NYPD officers rightfully receiving accident benefits when they suffer injuries on the job and are unable to work,” Shihata said in a statement. “But the [Police Pension Fund’s] current administration of these benefits is vulnerable to misuse and does not employ standards consistent with those used in similar law enforcement retirement systems, such as the system for state police.” Instead, the board has a single standard: whether an applicant can perform the general duties of a police officer, like subduing a suspect or operating a firearm — a threshold that makes less sense for officers with desk or administrative jobs. The report specifically cited the case of former Chief of Department John Chell, who was awarded a $295,919 annual pension while serving as the NYPD’s highest-ranking uniformed officer under former Mayor Eric Adams. The huge sum came, in part, because of an ankle injury sustained in 2024. Chell was among several top Adams-era police officials who received lucrative payouts using this criteria, which the DOI report argued contributed to mistrust in the system and the belief that higher-ranking officers had an easier time securing disability pay . (The report did not make any assumptions about whether Chell would have been granted his pension under stricter criteria.) DOI contends this standard incentivizes more people to claim a disability, citing a 2015 report that found 21% of NYPD employees retire on accident disability compared to 6% within the state system for police and firefighters, which has a more narrow criteria for awarding disability pay. Shihata even suggested that the pension board’s broad standard might not be legal, since courts have found, in the case of the state police pension rules, that job duty means what an officer actually does in practice. Despite that, the board rejected a DOI recommendation to change the standard. Notably, DOI pointed out in its report that two of the people on the medical board making the determinations are appointed by city agencies controlled by the mayor — which means Mayor Zohran Mamdani could push to overrule the board’s leadership. City Hall did not respond to a question about whether he would do so. The NYPD declined to comment, while the pension board did not respond. Chell could not be reached. The pension system does include a safeguard to maximize city resources. The board is authorized to re-examine officers receiving disability pensions who aren’t yet of retirement age to see if their condition would allow them to work a different city job, even if it’s not in the NYPD. If they’re deemed able, then they’re primarily compensated with their pension money until they reach retirement age. So is the pension system using this provision to examine the $100 million worth of annual pension payments doled out to NYPD officers who are under the retirement age, which the board is required by law to do? In short, no. Since 2019, the board has only reevaluated one pensioner, per the DOI report. And that person was found unable to do any other city work. The report found examples indicating the board could be doing a more thorough job. DOI provided findings that suggest four officers under the retirement age are receiving disability pensions while engaging in activities like lifting weights, performing home renovations, playing competitive sports, doing pushups, instructing workout classes and, in one case, performing “complicated dance routines exhibiting a full range of arm motion.” DOI recommended the board require officers receiving disability payments who are not yet of retirement age to periodically certify they still have a disability. The board rejected this recommendation, but agreed to create an online portal to gain input from the public on pensioners who may be healthy enough to work. It also agreed to reevaluate the four retirees flagged by DOI. — Joe Anuta From the Capitol META’S DAY IN COURT: New York’s top court opened its fall session this afternoon with a case that could have massive implications for the legal liability of social media companies and AI users. Website owners are typically immune from liability for content created by third parties. But the families of the 2022 mass shooting in Buffalo are arguing that social media companies shouldn’t dodge responsibility for radicalizing Payton Gendron, the 18-year-old who drove across the state with the goal of killing Black people. The state Court of Appeals is now deciding whether these families can proceed with a lawsuit against companies such as Meta, Google, Discord, Reddit, Amazon and 4Chan. Gendron’s diaries and confessions show he was motivated by white supremacist material he encountered while addicted to social media. The families contend these companies are liable because they intentionally designed an addictive algorithm that destroyed his mental health while proactively steering him to pro-violence content. “The social media companies had a role in causing the crime,” attorney Jennifer Bennett argued. “Heavy social media usage goes hand-in-hand with mass shootings.” Meta attorney Eric Shumsky said the entire argument boiled down to an attempt to sue over the actual content the shooter saw, a type of claim his company is protected against. “If the addiction were to cooking tutorials or cat videos or anything else, it would be an absolutely incoherent theory of liability,” Shumsky said. Judges on the seven-person court panel acknowledged the possibility of significant repercussions no matter how they rule. “Let’s say I can’t function, I can’t work anymore, because of my addiction to social media,” Judge Michael Garcia said while questioning the plaintiffs about how far reaching lawsuits might be under their theory. “It’s addictive, I can’t deal with people, I stay home, I can’t work.” “That is a viable claim,” Bennett said. “The evidence is very strong that the social media companies made a product to have this effect.” While questioning Meta, Chief Judge Rowan Wilson raised the possibility of troubling precedents if the court supports the idea of widespread immunity for app creators. “I use AI to, let’s say, ‘design me an app to create the most harm possible to teenagers,’” Wilson said. “It’s my intent to create an app that selects content designed to destroy the mental health of teenagers … Am I liable?” — Bill Mahoney EYES ON AI: Gov. Kathy Hochul chided the federal government today for not doing enough to address concerns about the existential threats artificial intelligence potentially poses. “Understandably, Americans are concerned, as am I,” Hochul told reporters after an event Tuesday in Manhattan. “We have an obligation to ensure that technological progress does not come at our own peril. So while Washington refuses to act, here in New York, we're stepping up.” Hochul pointed to the landmark RAISE Act , which goes into effect in January, and a one-year data center moratorium, which she issued in July, as evidence that New York is acting aggressively. Her administration earlier today rolled out a framework for communities that want to host a data center to minimize detrimental effects on the area. The governor added that she’ll find “additional actions that we can take at the state level to lead the way in the absence of leadership from Washington” — though she did not specify what that looks like. While some in Washington are eager to implement restrictions to slow down AI, President Donald Trump has tried to shut down those efforts , calling the AI dooming a “HOAX.” Hochul said she hasn’t had conversations with legislators in recent days regarding AI. — Madison Fernandez FROM CITY HALL TO ENFORCE OR NOT TO ENFORCE — THAT’S THE QUESTION: Mamdani wouldn’t commit today to ordering the NYPD to step up enforcement of traffic violations in New York City — because he’s focused on “behavioral change,” not punishment. The NYPD’s rate of issuing tickets to drivers who speed, blow through red lights, block bike lanes or otherwise break traffic laws remains far below pre-pandemic levels. And transit advocates, including left-leaning allies of Mamdani , say the police department must get back to issuing more violations, arguing that it’s critical to keeping city streets safe. This afternoon, though, Mamdani declined repeatedly to say whether he will deliver such marching orders to the NYPD and suggested enforcement isn’t a key priority for him. “Our goal here is not going to be measured in terms of the number of tickets that are issued or the violations, but rather behavioral change, and the NYPD is a partner in delivering that change,” Mamdani said, speaking at a press conference in Brooklyn held to unveil his new street safety plan , which contains ambitious proposals but is light on many implementation details. How does the city change behaviors without stepping up enforcement, though? In response to that question, Mamdani suggested the answer could lie in developing more protected bus and bike lanes and otherwise redesigning streets to make them safer for pedestrians. At the same time, Mamdani said he’s committed to “a continued partnership with the PD to use those tools of ticketing when any violation is present.” “We’re going to be taking a hard look at how best we can change behavior that we’re seeing in violation of street safety laws, and then utilize that. That includes the PD,” he said. The mayor’s comments came after Streetsblog reported the NYPD has shifted its traffic violation strategy to prioritize enforcement against scofflaws on e-bikes and other micromobility vehicles. That shift comes in spite of the fact that car drivers account for the vast majority of crashes and traffic deaths in the city, data shows. — Chris Sommerfeldt   FOILED ATTEMPT: The Manhattan Institute, a conservative think tank, is suing the Mamdani administration over its handling of Freedom of Information Law requests. The think tank has been seeking records related to meetings between foreign dignitaries and Ana María Archila, commissioner of the Mayor’s Office of International Affairs. Archila has faced criticism for attempting to meet with an Iranian diplomat amid that country’s war with the U.S. While the Adams administration provided tailored estimates for FOIL requests (but by no means fulfilled them in a timely manner), the institute found Mamdani’s City Hall team began giving out blanket six-month timetables for fulfilling requests. “City Hall has turned FOIL into a six-month waiting room for everyone,” Manhattan Institute City Policy Analyst Santiago Vidal Calvo and General Counsel Cameron Macdonald wrote in explaining their suit , which was filed in Manhattan Supreme Court. “That is why we are suing.” The city did not immediately respond to a request for comment about the lawsuit. — Joe Anuta SCREENS IN SCHOOLS: The New York City public school system banned unfettered access to YouTube on school-issued devices for the current school year, the Department of Education revealed Tuesday. The ban — which went into effect last week, ahead of the first day of school — comes amid calls from City Council members to limit the use of YouTube, personal devices and AI in the classroom. “We heard everyone loud and clear,” DOE official Scott Strickland said at a Council hearing today. “As of Wednesday night at 5 p.m., we filtered YouTube out of all student devices. They shouldn’t be able to access it either on a Chromebook or an iPad both at school and at home.” Council member Shekar Krishnan, who chairs the Council’s Oversight and Investigations Committee and was co-leading Tuesday’s hearing, said he was “very glad to hear” of the YouTube ban. Educational videos embedded into Google Classroom for specific lessons will be exempt from the ban. Earlier this month, Mamdani announced a year-long AI moratorium for students in grades 2-K through eighth grade. Hochul and lawmakers in Albany also rolled out a full-day “bell-to-bell” restriction on cellphone use during the school day last school year. Ahead of this afternoon’s hearing, Krishnan and Council member Eric Dinowitz, who chairs the Education Committee, held a rally railing against screen-heavy classroom instruction and calling, among other things, for a YouTube ban. “We will not let the greed of big technology companies get in the way of our children's future and their education," Krishnan said at the rally. — Molly Reinmann IN OTHER NEWS — DECLASSIFIED DOCS: Trump said he’d consider releasing classified documents related to 9/11 after victims’ families pleaded for clarity on Saudi Arabia’s involvement. ( NY Post ) — TIED UP: Long Island Democratic House candidate Christopher Gallant acknowledged he posed in bondage gear for an ad campaign over a decade ago. ( The New York Times ) — ICE ARRESTS: Police in the Westchester village of Port Chester have turned over more people with no criminal record to ICE than other local law enforcement agencies, despite assertions the police department would not cooperate with ICE. articles.body: Texas Republicans were already fretting about slipping support with voters of color. Then Bo French got on X. The Republican nominee for Texas Railroad Commissioner posted a photo of a crowd of University of Texas football fans, most of them people of color, saying , “The problem is now obviously far worse than anyone imagined.” The Sunday morning comments, which appeared to target South Asian students, sent Lone Star Republicans into a frenzy, worried about the impact the rhetoric could have on GOP candidates up and down the ballot, including Attorney General Ken Paxton’s high-profile Senate race and Texas Gov. Greg Abbott’s reelection fight. A number of Republican lawmakers, including some in tough races, quickly denounced the post as racist, as others squirmed with carefully worded statements. And GOP operatives winced at the potential electoral backlash — in a year that’s already looking tougher-than-normal for a party that has dominated the state for decades. Still, no one explicitly called for him to drop out of the race. “His post on social media is profoundly unhelpful if his goal is to see Republicans win statewide races in a tough political environment in 50 days,” said Matt Mackowiak, an Austin-based GOP consultant who advised Sen. John Cornyn’s (R-Texas) unsuccessful primary campaign against Paxton. Cornyn condemned the post , asking whether other GOP officials would “condemn the intolerance and racism, or look the other way while it becomes normalized.” Rep. Monica De La Cruz (R-Texas), who is facing a tough reelection fight in a Hispanic-majority district, told POLITICO in a statement she’s willing to “condemn racism” wherever it comes from. "All I see in that photograph is a group of kids celebrating a Longhorns win. What can be more Texan than that?” De La Cruz said, before taking a shot at her Democratic opponent, Bobby Pulido, for his past racial comments . And Karl Rove, a longtime adviser to former President George W. Bush, called French a “bigot” at a private lunch event and said he’s voting for French’s Democratic opponent, The Texas Tribune reported . Meanwhile, state Rep. Jon Rosenthal, the Democrat running against French, said he had his best fundraising day of the cycle after French’s post. French didn’t respond to requests for comment. He repeatedly stood by his comments since Sunday morning. During a local radio appearance Monday, he said he didn’t have any personal animosity against the students at the football game, but said that it is “not racist to point out that we should be favoring Texans over foreigners” and that his fellow Republicans are afraid of being called racist . The divide emerging among Texas Republicans over the social media post — and Democrats’ eagerness to capitalize on it — show just how precarious the party finds its position this cycle. Texas Republicans were already worrying about losing support from Hispanic and other minority voters amid a tough economic environment and President Donald Trump’s unpopular immigration agenda. They need to hold onto or improve the incremental gains they made over previous cycles with voters of color in a fast-changing state where non-Hispanic white people now only make up 37% of the population. The stakes are high this cycle: Most polls show Paxton slightly trailing in a Senate race that could determine control of the upper chamber; Abbott appears to be in the toughest of his four election fights; and the state is home to several key House races. “I don’t think [French’s post] independently and universally sours voter sentiment. But it contributes to GOP declining numbers with Hispanic voters particularly in the South Texas congressional races which we hope to win,” said Alfredo Rodriguez, a Dallas-based Republican strategist, who called on French to “stop the petty political theatrics.” The blast radius of French’s posts was wide enough to garner carefully worded responses from the top of the ticket. Abbott said in a Sunday statement that French’s post “is not my message,” before noting unity “doesn’t mean that Texas cannot also lead in having the toughest immigration laws of any state in America and freezing H1B visas at our universities.” Two of the students in the photo told the Dallas Morning News that they’re U.S. citizens . Most UT students are Texans — state law requires that 90% of each freshman class come from in-state — and there is no evidence that the students in the photo French posted are foreigners. Some Republicans weren’t thrilled about Abbott’s response. “This had nothing to do with illegal immigrants,” said Anang Mittal, an Indian American national GOP strategist, of Abbott’s comments. “These were students at a college game. They're not H-1B. If they're students, they're on a student visa. … It's pretty damn disgusting of Greg Abbott to say, ‘I condemn racism, but also, like, we're keeping all the Indians out.’ That's essentially what that tweet read to me.” Democrat James Talarico called Paxton out on social media, asking if he would follow Cornyn’s lead in denouncing French’s post. The GOP nominee replied that he condemns “racism in all its forms” — and then claimed Talarico had a “history of dividing Texans by race.” Spokespeople for Paxton and Abbott did not respond to requests for comment. Other Republicans were less willing to fully denounce French’s comments. “I don't really know the guy. I heard he said some not so pleasant things,” said Rep. Troy Nehls (R-Texas), who said he hadn’t seen the posts — but launched into a criticism of immigration nonetheless. “I am concerned about the number of people living in this country, and we don't even know who they really are,” he said. ”Shut the border down for 10 years, and then let's try to figure out who we got in this country because we don't even know." Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.), who campaigned with Talarico in Houston on Sunday, said French’s posts came up in conversations with every Asian American voter he met. “Everyone was talking about it,” Kim said. “Every single Asian American that I was with yesterday raised this with me. They were saying this is an example of, ‘Not only are they not courting us or engaging with us, but they’re actively demonizing us, actively being xenophobic and racist towards us.’ We need leaders that stand up against this.” The political damage could also extend — potentially for years — to Texas’ small but growing Indian American population, the demographic group French appeared to target in his posts. Both Dallas and Houston have significant Indian American populations. In 2019, an event at a Houston stadium headlined by Trump and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi drew over 50,000 attendees. French’s comments could alienate those same voters, said Brendan Steinhauser, a Republican consultant in Austin. “He just irritated a bunch of people, many of whom could be supporters and could be Republicans,” said Steinhauser, a University of Texas graduate. “I'd be willing to bet a lot of those kids that he was posting a photo of are probably, you know, their parents might be Republicans, or they might be Republicans, or conservatives, or independent-leaning conservatives.” If French is elected, he would sit on a commission that regulates Texas’ powerful oil, gas and mining industries — which has little to do with immigration or social issues. But French, a longtime provocateur in Texas political circles, has a history of incendiary statements. Just last year, Republicans were calling on French to resign as chair of the Tarrant County Republican Party after he published an online poll asking whether Muslims or Jews were “the bigger threat to America.” He deleted the post and said he regretted it, adding “antisemitism has no place in the Republican Party.” This spring, he unseated a well-financed Republican incumbent for Texas Railroad Commission. French isn’t the only politician in Texas who has made singling out Muslims part of his political brand. Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick has made “preventing Shariah law in Texas” one of his legislative priorities. Patrick didn’t respond to a request for comment. Abbott, Paxton and Cornyn have all called for investigations and other government action to stop development of a commercial and residential development being built by the East Plano Islamic Center, a mosque outside Dallas . And just last month, Abbott threatened to withhold funding from Dallas Fort Worth International Airport to block plans for ritual washing facilities for Muslim travelers in the airport’s terminals. There’s little difference between French’s attacks and the other politicians’ actions, said Yasir Qadhi, an Islamic scholar at the Islamic center.“It is the same mindset,” he said in an interview. “What we're witnessing is really an unprecedented and increasingly brazen form of racism. It's unfiltered, it's unapologetic, it's even stripped of even the pretense of political correctness. You know, this is a type of racism we've never seen in our lifetimes.” When French unleashed a string of inflammatory social media posts in 2025, several GOP officeholders — including Patrick, the lieutenant governor — called on him to resign as county GOP chair. But Republicans now refuse to tell French to drop out now “because that might mean that there would be a Democrat elected statewide,” said Glen Whitley, a Republican former Tarrant County judge. “That's the bottom line.” “That's part of my frustration with the Republican Party altogether: They talk about being Christian, but they get up every morning to talk about who they hate,” said Whitley, who still identifies as Republican but endorsed Talarico for Senate. Joey Fox contributed to this report.

articles.body: NEW YORK — A state lawmaker who gained national attention for his opposition to unchecked AI during a failed campaign for Congress this year is launching a $30 million effort to unite Democrats around regulating the technology, according to the organization’s new website. New York Assemblymember Alex Bores is unveiling the organization — called “Who Decides” — on Tuesday to “build the winning Democratic answer to AI,” according to a website that was publicly available Monday night. “Who Decides’ goal is that by 2028, Democratic candidates from the top of the ticket on down run with a common AI safety agenda,” reads an announcement on the site dated Tuesday . “That means addressing the harms people already see and the broader danger that increasingly powerful and out-of-control systems could destabilize our economy, our democracy, and our safety.” It was not immediately clear whether Who Decides would be organized as a federal super PAC, 501(c)(4) nonprofit or other type of group. The website has a “donate” link that redirects to a webpage hosted by “Give Butter,” an organization focused on helping nonprofits fundraise. The announcement said the group would reject “corporate money or contributions from senior executives at frontier AI companies.” Bores did not immediately respond to questions about the organization Monday night, including whether Bores, a sitting state lawmaker, personally fundraised for the group while holding public office. He is launching the organization with his former chief of staff, Anna Myers, the website says. The apparent launch of Who Decides comes at a moment when the quickly-advancing technology has become a major political issue. Last week, a former Anthropic researcher issued a dire warning that artificial intelligence has a chance of bringing about the end of humanity. The concerns from the researcher, Jacob Coxon, who also worked for OpenAI, were followed up by calls from the leaders of Anthropic and OpenAI, along with Elon Musk, to regulate the industry and slow development to build more guardrails. Politicians have scrambled to respond, with both parties trying to coalesce around a policy agenda — and political message — on the rapidly evolving issue. Former President Barack Obama called last week for Democrats to focus on AI , and prominent party strategists from across the ideological spectrum gathered to begin mapping out a strategy . President Donald Trump rejected recent calls from Republicans and Democrats to quickly regulate the industry in a spate of Monday social media posts . “We don’t let five people write the laws for hundreds of millions of Americans,” Bores says in the launch announcement on the website, an apparent reference to the top executives in the AI industry. “There is no reason to let them write the rules for AI.” The group says on the site it will focus on 11 states that it says will be key to the 2028 presidential primary and general election: South Carolina, Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, Virginia, Arizona, Georgia, North Carolina, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin. It says it will conduct quarterly national and state polls, host national conferences and partner with local groups in the states. Earlier this year, Bores lost the primary for retiring Manhattan Democratic Rep. Jerry Nadler’s seat. His campaign largely centered on a push to regulate artificial intelligence following his work to pass the RAISE Act in the state Legislature, which aimed to enact safeguards for the technology. His campaign attracted a combined $21 million from super PACs backed by dueling factions of the AI community, which spent both in support and opposition of him. Democratic Assemblymember Micah Lasher ultimately won the primary and is all but assured to win in November in the deep-blue seat. “The lesson Bores and Myers took from those fights was that confronting the AI industry is fertile political ground and that public demand for answers on AI policy exists but remains scattered,” the website said, referencing his congressional campaign. “What’s missing is a coalition capable of turning that energy into a governing consensus before the technology, the economic dislocation, and the partisan battle lines harden.”

articles.body: La que va ser la primera síndica de greuges de Barcelona, Pilar Malla , ha mort aquest dimecres, 16 de setembre, als 95 anys. La mateixa sindicatura ha informat del seu decés a través de les xarxes socials. 2004 va ser nomenada la primera síndica de la ciutat per l’aleshores alcalde Joan Clos i va estar en el càrrec durant sis anys, fins al 2010 . “Pilar Malla va obrir camí” “Acomiadem amb tristesa qui va posar els primers fonaments de la institució”, destaquen des de la Sindicatura en un comunicat. I afegeixen: “Pilar Malla va obrir camí. Va contribuir a fer de la queixa ciutadana una expressió de normalitat democràtica i va defensar el dret de tothom a ser escoltat i a rebre respostes clares de l’Administració”. I destaquen que Malla va iniciar “una manera d’entendre la sindicatura” basada en el fet d’escoltar, acompanyar i defensar els drets dels ciutadans, “especialment quan més ho necessiten”. Ens ha deixat la Pilar Malla, primera síndica de Barcelona. Va obrir camí en la defensa dels drets i la dignitat de les persones, sempre al costat de les més vulnerabilitzades. Una manera d’actuar que avui és llegat. Gràcies per tant, Pilar. https://t.co/4Joc3xjqRP — Sindicatura de Greuges de Barcelona (@sindicaturabcn) September 17, 2026 Va dirigir Càritas de Barcelona durant cinc anys Abans de la sindicatura, Malla també va ser cap dels Serveis Socials de la Generalitat entre 1989 i 1998 i va dirigir Càritas Diocesana de Barcelona durant cinc anys, de 1993 a 1998. També va formar part del Consell Municipal de Benestar Social de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, i l’any 1999 va ser elegida diputada del Parlament com a membre de Ciutadans pel Canvi a les llistes del PSC. Al llarg de la seva trajectòria ha estat guardonada amb el Memorial Joan XXIII per la Pau (1985), el Premi d’Honor Lluís Carulla (1988), la Creu d’Or de l’orde civil de la Solidaritat Social del Govern espanyol (1996) i la Creu de Sant Jordi (2004). També et pot interessar El Ple avala que David Bondia repeteixi com a síndic de greuges de Barcelona durant cinc anys més Roger Torres i Liñán 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: Aquest diumenge, 20 de setembre, es disputarà la Cursa de la Mercè 2026, que podràs seguir en directe aquí a betevé . Doncs aquesta 48a edició arriba amb rècord pel que fa a inscrits. De fet, s’han esgotat tots els dorsals disponibles de la cursa de 10 km que va posar a disposició l’organització, tants com 17.200. Més de 17.000 inscrits a la Cursa de la Mercè 2026 La Cursa de la Mercè tornarà a omplir de corredors els carrers de Barcelona. I aquest cop s’ha superat el nombre d’inscrits de les gairebé cinquantena edicions que s’han disputat fins ara. L’organització va marcar-se el límit de 17.200 dorsals i a hores d’ara ja s’han exhaurit tots els de la cursa de 10 km, que eren 16.000, i també els de la cursa familiar, que eren 1.200 i que també s’han exhaurit. A aquests, cal afegir els atletes que participaran a la cursa 2k inclusiva. També et pot interessar Cursa de la Mercè 2026: Data, horari, recorregut i inscripcions i tota la informació de la prova Amb aquestes xifres se supera el millor registre d’inscrits d’una Cursa de la Mercè que data de l’any 2013 , quan s’hi van inscriure 17.000 corredors . A més, també s’han venut més dorsals que l’any passat. L’any 2025 van participar-hi 14.500 atletes . Per tant, la Cursa de la Mercè 2026 arriba amb rècord, rècord d’inscrits.

articles.body: La consellera d’Interior, Núria Parlon , ha justificat el moment en què es van enviar els dos ES-Alert a la població per alertar-la de l’episodi de pluges d’aquest dimecres a la nit. En roda de premsa ha explicat que l’avís s’envia a la població o bé de forma preventiva —com la setmana passada— quan hi ha un avís d’alerta vermella; o bé quan hi ha un canvi en la situació meteorològica que pot posar en risc la ciutadania, com ha passat aquesta darrera nit. És a dir, que l’alerta es va enviar quan el Meteocat va corregir la previsió i va elevar els avisos al nivell màxim de 6 sobre 6. “No és que arribi tard sinó en el moment en què la població s’ha de protegir”, argumenta. També et pot interessar Una tromba d’aigua provoca inundacions i afectacions al metro i la ronda de Dalt Mar Arans 1 minut de lectura Parlon ha estat taxativa a l’explicar el perquè no es va enviar abans l’avís: “No enviarem un ES-Alert a la població per dir que plou molt, ni pararem el país per dir que plou molt”. La consellera argumenta que aquests avisos “no s’envien alegrement” , sinó quan cal prendre mesures de protecció perquè, si no, “al final la gent no faria cas”. També et pot interessar Servei parcial a l’L4 i l’L11 del metro i diverses afectacions a l’aeroport i Rodalies pels aiguats Jessica Moreno Cusac Marta Casals Torres 3 minuts de lectura El partit del Barça no va perillar Des d’Interior també han valorat el fet que durant l’enviament de les alertes estigués disputant el partit del Barça-Racing al Camp Nou. “Si haguéssim enviat un Es-Alert a les 19 h ningú no hauria acceptat que se suspengués el partit del Barça”, ha dit Parlon. Per la consellera l’enviament de l’alerta durant el partit és útil “perquè quan acabi no agafis el vehicle, t’esperis o no assumeixis riscos que poden anar contra la teva seguretat”. El subdirector general de Protecció Civil, Sergio Delgado , també ha explicat que, en cap moment, van fer la proposta de suspendre el matx . Argumenta que l’activitat del partit ja estava en marxa i que si les afectacions haguessin estat greus haurien valorar mesures com endarrerir la sortida dels assistents. articles.body: El temps no acabarà de fer net aquest dijous, malgrat que ja no s’espera pluja intensa. La previsió del temps anuncia un matí força rúfol, amb algun plugim, i una tarda més tranquil·la amb força estones de sol. Previsió horària per a Barcelona 11 h: núvols i possibilitat d’alguna gota 15 h: possibilitat d’algun plugim 19 h: moltes clarianes, estones de sol 21 h: sensació de tardor plena També et pot interessar L’estiu del 2026 ha deixat 19 dies addicionals de calor extrema a Barcelona i 41 a Madrid Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura Matí gris, tarda amb estones de sol La matinada ha estat clarament més fresca que l’anterior. Matí de cel força ennuvolat i encara amb alguns xàfecs damunt del mar , a tocar la costa. No es descarta algun xàfec curt o plugim fins al migdia al litoral barceloní. Les clarianes aniran a més havent dinat. Cel força clar avançada la tarda. Clar descens de la temperatura màxima. Matí insegur, amb algun xàfec breu o plugim al litoral, sobretot al sud de l’entorn metropolità. Pluja forta damunt del mar, no es descarta que fregui la costa en algun sector del litoral barceloní. articles.body: Els efectes dels forts aiguats d’aquest dimecres encara es noten en el transport públic. El servei de metro ha arrencat aquest dijous amb servei parcial a la Línia 4 , que funciona entre la Pau i Verdaguer . Segons ha informat TMB a través de les xarxes socials, s’ha habilitat un bus alternatiu per cobrir el trajecte entre les estacions de Verdaguer i la Trinitat Nova. Aquest servei està registrant llargues cues , sobretot a primera hora del matí, tot i que la freqüència de pas dels vehicles és cada cinc minuts. TMB recomana com a alternativa utilitzar la línia d’autobús D50 , que realitza el mateix recorregut. Segons la companyia de transports, l’L11 només funciona entre Can Cuiàs i Ciutat Meridiana i l’andana central de Fabra i Puig es troba sense servei. També et pot interessar Una tromba d’aigua provoca inundacions i afectacions al metro i la ronda de Dalt Mar Arans 1 minut de lectura Afectacions a l’aeroport i Rodalies L’aeroport de Barcelona també arrossega la ressaca del temporal, amb almenys una vintena de vols cancel·lats i alguns retards . A l’ R2, l’R2 Nord i l’R11 s’ha interromput la circulació a entre Sant Andreu i Montcada per un arrossegament de les pedres que hi ha sota la via a causa de les pluges. Es tracta d’un punt proper a l’esvoranc de Vallbona i Adif haurà de formigonar la zona. Renfe ha establert un servei directe per carretera entre Granollers i Sant Andreu com alternativa. Se encuentra suspendida la circulación entre Sant Andreu y Granollers Centre, de las líneas R2 y R2 Nord del núcleo de Rodalies de Catalunya, por una avería en la vía. articles.body: Amb l’impuls econòmic de les diferents administracions implicades, la Sagrera i els seus entorns veuen com la finalització de les obres de la futura estació d’alta velocitat i el parc lineal és cada vegada més a prop de ser una realitat. Això, segons ha destacat la regidora andreuenca Marta Villanueva a l’ Infobarris , converteix Sant Andreu en el districte cridat a ser la nova centralitat de la ciutat. Es tracta d’un àmbit d’actuació de prop de 165 hectàrees , on s’espera que durant els propers anys hi aterrin 25.000 veïns , que viuran en els 11.000 nous habitatges projectats, gairebé la meitat dels quals dotacionals. També et pot interessar Barcelona invertirà 260 M € per transformar l’entorn de l’estació de la Sagrera i “acabar la ciutat” Marina Segura i Vidal 3 minuts de lectura “És l’obra civil més gran de tot l’estat” Villanueva no ha dubtat a qualificar els treballs que s’estan executant a la Sagrera com “ l’obra civil més gran que s’està fent a tot l’estat “. Ha reconegut que es tracta d’un projecte que ha comportat molts problemes al conjunt d’actors implicats per la gran quantitat d’entrebancs que ha patit, però amb tot, veu que acabarà aviat: “La transformació urbanística la veurem abans del que ens pensem”. Recordem, les previsions són les de tenir acabada l’estació de cara l’ any 2032 i les primeres promocions d’habitatges enllestides d’aquí a dos o tres anys. Més enllà, la regidora ha volgut subratllar les transformacions que patiran altres zones, com ara la rambla de Prim, o el Bon Pastor, amb el desenvolupament de la cinquena fase. Però sens dubte, la gran joia serà el futur “ecodistricte”, que ocuparà els antics terrenys de la fàbrica Mercedes-Benz , on es preveu que hi hagi 1.300 nous habitatges . En conjunt, parlem d’una àrea de dimensions faraòniques que tindrà 84.000 m² de complexos hotelers; 480.000 m², de nova activitat econòmica i 200.000 m², destinats a nous equipaments. Filant més prim, Villanueva ha projectat “ nous equipaments esportius, dos nous centres d’atenció primària “, entre d’altres. També hi ha previstes diverses escoles bressol més, residències per a gent gran, instituts de formació professional, centres cívics i culturals, així com un emplaçament de reconeixement per a la memòria històrica d’aquest espai. Reallotjament de la Trinitat Nord Una de les novetats que ha explicat la regidora és la reformulació del conveni del projecte Trinitat Nord . Es tracta de tots aquells veïns que viuen en els coneguts com a habitatges del Patronat, als voltants de l’antiga presó de dones de la Trinitat Vella. Són uns habitatges afectats pel projecte d’enderroc del centre penitenciari i la construcció d’una nova promoció d’habitatge. Fins a principis d’estiu, només un terç de tot aquest veïnat tenia dret a reallotjament a les noves llars en aplicació de la llei d’urbanisme, però ara, gràcies a les converses entre Ajuntament i entitats, “s’espera que la gran majoria puguin ser reallotjats “, ha confirmat Villanueva. També et pot interessar Veïns expropiats de pisos del Patronat a la Trinitat Vella: “Si cal, tallarem el nus de la Trinitat” Max Sagués 2 minuts de lectura Actuacions imminents al distircte Finalment, la regidora ha tingut temps per remarcar destacar diverses actuacions que es preveuen “imminents” al districte. En primer lloc, la pintura de la nova zona verda a la Trinitat Vella , una reivindicació llargament exigida per un barri que fa anys que és víctima de l’anomenat park & ride . Fins ara, molta gent vinguda de fora de la ciutat aprofitava la presència d’aparcament gratuït per estacionar el seu vehicle al barri durant el dia i desplaçar-se per la ciutat amb transport públic, això deixava sense places lliures els veïns. En segon lloc, l’obertura al complet del nou CEM Sagrera . Després d’un any i mig de retard en la inauguració de la seva piscina, aquest estiu, els veïns dels entorns han pogut gaudir de la seva frescor. Després de l’adjudicació de la gestió a l’empresa Agora Meeting Sport Place quedava saber quan es donaria el tret de sortida a la resta d’activitats que s’han de dur a terme en aquest equipament. Tot i no concretar una data, Villanueva ha dit que únicament queda “ dotar a les sales de les màquines “, de manera que durant les properes setmanes ja podria estar tot enllestit. L’entrevista sencera de l’ Infobarris

articles.body: El Festival Internacional de Cinema i Art de Barcelona, el Dart Festival 2026, celebrarà el desè aniversari. El festival en el format habitual es farà del 26 al 28 de novembre als Cinemes Bosque . Però, atenció, per l’aniversari hi haurà una programació especial amb 10 projeccions a diferents districtes que es faran del 8 d’octubre al 25 de novembre . Aquí pots veure l’avançament del programa i més endavant t’ampliarem la informació. Dates del festival Dart especial arquitectura (gratuït) Del 8 d’octubre al 25 de novembre . El primer tram del festival serà gratuït amb les projeccions de 10 pel·lícules als diferents districtes. Gratuït. Pel·lícula inaugural – 8 d’octubre El festival s’inaugurarà a la Casa de l’Arquitectura de Barcelona (antiga seu de l’Editorial Gustavo Gili) en el marc de la Capital Mundial de l’Arquitectura Barcelona 2026. La pel·lícula que es projectarà sera Out of the picture . Festival Dart 2026 26, 27 i 28 de novembre . Les pel·lícules del Festival de Cinema i Arts Visuals de Barcelona es podran veure als cinemes Bosque i seran de pagament. Programa Dart especial arquitectura (gratuït) Aquí tens la programació gratuïta. Per veure les pel·lícules cal reserva prèvia al web del festival. Jornada inaugural 8 d’octubre, a les 19 h Out of the picture , d’An.Ash Smolar Meynart (estrena a Espanya) El documental explora la invisibilització de les dones a la història de l’arquitectura, una disciplina dominada per homes durant molt de temps, a través del testimoni de Denise Scott Brown i d’altres arquitectes, historiadores i investigadores. A l’antiga Casa de l’Arquitectura (antiga seu de l’editorial Gustavo Gili) , a l’Eixample . Les altres projeccions gratuïtes 16 d’octubre, a les 19 h Josep Lluís Sert, un sueño nómada , de Pablo Bujosa. Centre Cívic Joan Oliver – Pere Quart (les Corts) 20 d’octubre, a les 19 h The women of the Bauhaus , de Susanne Radelhof + Where we grow older , de Daniel Schwartz. Curt . (estrena a Espanya). Lleialtat Santsenca (Sants-Montjuïc). El curtmetratge Where we grow older explora com l’envelliment de la població està transformant l’arquitectura, l’urbanisme i les polítiques de cures, a través de projectes pioners a Barcelona i Baltimore, que imaginen noves formes de viure la longevitat des de la comunitat i el disseny dels espais. 24 d’octubre, a les 17.30 h Charlotte Perriand, pionnière de l’art de vivre , de Stéphane Ghez. Tòtem, de Macià Florit Campins. Curt . Fundació Joan Miró (Sants-Montjuïc). 4 de novembre, a les 18.30 h Concrete forms of resistance , de Nick Jordan (estrena a Espanya). Curt . Re-Destruction, de Simon El Habre (estrena a Espanya). Centre Cívic Pati Llimona (Ciutat Vella). 10 de novembre, a les 18 h The Cathedral , de Denis Dobrovoda + Cénotaphe , de Catherine Aventurier (estrena a Espanya). Curts . Biblioteca Vilapicina i la Torre Llobeta- Carmen Laforet (Nou Barris).   The Cathedral retrata la insòlita història de Justo Gallego, que va dedicar 60 anys a construir, tot sol i amb materials reciclats, una catedral monumental als afores de Madrid. A Cénotaphe l’escultora francesa Eva Jospin, crea un monument funerari enorme a l’abadia romana de Montmajour. Sota una llum daurada, Jospin dona vida a una obra espectacular i delicada, fruit d’un treball artesanal minuciós que transforma un material purament utilitari com el cartró en una escultura monumental i, alhora, fràgil, gairebé com una teranyina. 12 de novembre, a les 19 h Radical Landscapes , d’Elettra Fiumi. Centre Cívic Ateneu Fort Pienc (Eixample). La cineasta Elettra Fiumi descobreix als arxius del seu pare el llegat oblidat del col·lectiu radical 9999. Amb un viatge entre Florència, els Estats Units, el Swinging London i el Canadà de l’Expo de Montreal, el documental recupera l’esperit psicodèlic, irreverent i transformador d’una generació que va desafiar el racionalisme i el funcionalisme dominants. 17 de novembre, a les 19 h Green over Gray : Emilio Ambasz , de Francesca Molteni, Mattia Colombo (estrena a Catalunya). ECHO , de Boa Mistura. Curt . Ca l’Alier (Sant Martí). 19 de novembre, a les 19 h Out of the picture , d’An.Ash Smolar Meynart (projecció per cortesia de Thank You and Goodnight Production i Atelier Graphoui). La pel·lícula revisita 50 anys després dels habitatges experimentals concebuts per tres arquitectes belgues arran del Maig del 68. articles.body: La sorpresa i les alarmes van saltar quan fa uns dies va sortir a la llum que des del 2024 les més de nou hectàrees de La Ponderosa, la darrera finca agrícola de la ciutat, pertany a Aigües de Barcelona. La companyia no ha anunciat quin és l’objectiu de la compra, però l’ Ajuntament ja ha manifestat el rebuig al projecte d’una planta potabilitzadora. La tinenta d’alcaldia d’Ecologia i Urbanisme, Laia Bonet, ha assegurat que defensen la necessitat d’aquest tipus d’infraestructures hidràuliques que facin l’àrea metropolitana més resilient a la sequera, però no a costa dels horts de La Ponderosa. “No és el lloc adequat”. Així, va apuntar que ja fa temps que han parlat amb les administracions i ens implicats, com l’Agència Catalana de l’Aigua (ACA), la Generalitat i l’Àrea Metropolitana de Barcelona (AMB) per expressar el seu neguit. “No ens hem limitat a dir que no, hem treballat per posar sobre la taula ubicacions alternatives , perquè es faci en un altre lloc sense comprometre un espai tan estratègic com és La Ponderosa”, ha afirmat Laia Bonet després de ser interpel·lada per aquesta qüestió pels comuns a la Comissió d’Ecologia, Urbanisme, Mobilitat i Habitatge. També et pot interessar L’Ajuntament blindarà l’última finca agrícola de la ciutat per transformar Vallbona en un ecobarri Lluís Cruz Berasategui 3 minuts de lectura La Ponderosa, per al barri Amb espai estratègic, Bonet fa referència al projecte socioeconòmic Agrovallbona, planejat el 2023 com una manera de blindar els horts i oferir noves oportunitats al veïnat de Vallbona, amb, entre altres coses, un espai de formació i recerca aplicat a l’agroecologia, a més d’altres aspectes més comunitaris. Aquest projecte implicava la requalificació de la finca de sòl urbanitzable a sòl agrícola, una protecció molt reivindicada des del territori. Però els planejaments no han arribat a temps. Tanmateix, l’Ajuntament defensa que La Ponderosa ha d’estar lligada al barri. “El futur de La Ponderosa s’ha de decidir posant al centre les necessitats del barri, les oportunitats dels veïns i la qualitat de vida de la Zona Nord”, afegeix Laia Bonet. “La Ponderosa és una oportunitat per a Vallbona”.

articles.body: La intel·ligència artificial posarà en risc la humanitat? Hi ha un perill imminent per al nostre futur? Fins quin punt pot arribar a canviar les nostres vides ? Al programa bàsics , de betevé, Karina Gibert , catedràtica de la UPC experta en IA i degana del COEINF, i Arnau Font , divulgador especialitzat en tecnologia i IA, han respost aquestes preguntes i d’altres, com ara l’impacte que poden tenir aquestes eines i quina regulació caldria aplicar-hi. Karina Gibert ha assegurat que la IA no se’ns escapa de les mans i matisa: “El que se’ns està escapant de les mans és el seny”. Gibert explica que, al cap i a la fi, es pot desenvolupar sota uns marcs de comportament , connectar-la i desconnectar-la segons convingui, però ha volgut recalcar: “Ningú explica quins són els límits , és com vendre un medicament sense prospecte “. És per això que considera les últimes notícies sobre el perill de la IA per a la humanitat com a “ bombes mediàtiques “ perquè tothom parli d’això. Font, per la seva banda, també considera que hi ha un component de màrqueting molt rellevant. Tot i això, el divulgador ha definit l’arribada de la intel·ligència artificial generativa com una revolució industrial molt més ràpida que les anteriors. També et pot interessar Daniel Calleja: “Barcelona té una oportunitat extraordinària amb la IA” Cristina Brotons 3 minuts de lectura Les regulacions per a “un tràiler sense fre” Tots dos han comentat també què opinen de la regulació que, sens dubte, acabarà arribant per controlar aquestes eines . De fet, Gibert ho ha exemplificat amb el símil d’un vehicle remolcat: “Si el deixes anar sense fre, és clar que és perillós”. Si bé coincideixen en el fet que caldrà regular la IA , els experts demanen controlar com es farà. “Si els que han de posar les regles del joc són els mateixos que han de fer el negoci, no tinc molt clar que acabem regulant de la manera adequada “, ha sentenciat la catedràtica de la UPC. També et pot interessar Una empresa barcelonina crea una plataforma d’intel·ligència artificial per a mestres Jordi Escofet 1 minut de lectura Els riscos per als joves i un pla de formació Karina Gibert ha apuntat també que utilitzar la IA és com un carnet : “Hauries de tenir certs coneixements per fer-la servir”. A banda, ha reclamat que es dissenyi un pla de formació en competències digitals que comenci en nens petits perquè aprenguin a fer-la servir esquivant els riscos que pot comportar-ne l’ús. Sobre això, Arnau Font ha afegit que la necessitat de formació també es pot aplicar a pares i docents . Recupera la taula completa
